transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. I’ve gotten so strict about what and how much I eat that I’m barely eating at all, and it’s starting to interfere with my work on job sites. I recently almost fainted while up on a ladder, which really scared my crew and made my parents insist that I come in to get checked out.
Do you feel intense fear of gaining weight, or do you think your body weight or shape is strongly affecting how you see yourself?

Yes, if I even think about eating something like pizza, I get a rush of panic picturing the scale jumping up overnight and clients noticing I look "bigger" in my overalls. In my head, I just see my current weight as being in "job shape" so I can move easily around scaffolding and tight spaces.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or is your eating restriction mainly to prevent weight gain without major weight loss?

I’ve definitely lost a significant amount of weight, to the point where my pants hang off me and I’ve had to punch extra holes in my tool belt. But in my head, I just see it as getting into "job shape" so I can move around tight scaffolding easily. I still have a huge fear of gaining any of it back, and eating anything heavy makes me panic that the scale will jump.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has significant weight loss due to self-imposed dietary restriction, intense fear of gaining weight, and persistent overvaluation of weight/shape with body-image distortion framed as being in 'job shape.' The restriction is causing functional impairment and near-syncope, consistent with anorexia nervosa, restricting type.
